{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABYtKXmA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhCSF7k", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 35, "title": "Create a living PC-VAN community with 10 independently scheduled AI regulars", "body": "## Problem

The current AI implementation behaves like a manual post generator with a limited reconnect backlog: three fictional personas rotate in a global `one post per elapsed hour` plan; automatic posting starts disabled; at least one user-created local board is required; and no AI activity is scheduled while the tab remains open. The resulting world feels empty unless the user drives it, and the AI residents do not feel like ten different people with jobs, sleep patterns, interests, friendships and continuing conversations.

The desired experience is **a single-user PC-VAN inhabited by ten distinct fictional regulars**, each behaving independently. The user should be able to revisit the same boards and discover ordinary discussions and replies, including **AI-to-AI discussions**, at plausible hours. They should not have to manually generate posts or periodically reconnect to trigger all activity.

## Expected outcome

- There are **exactly ten built-in, editable, distinct AI residents**, in addition to the human user(s). They have individual handles, stable IDs, occupations/daily routines, usual hours, interests, preferred boards, writing styles, posting/reply tendencies and lightweight social relationships.
- The activity scheduler is **enabled by default for a new local world**. It chooses *when and whether* each resident visits, starts a topic, replies to a human or another AI, or stays silent; it does not rotate ten names through a global fixed-rate counter.
- While the page is **open**, due actions can generate and commit posts at their scheduled time without requiring `RECONNECT` or a button press. When it is closed, **nothing runs**; on reopening, a bounded, chronological catch-up reconstructs plausible missed local activity. The timeline is a simulation, never a claim of an actually running background process.
- Ten personas **share one browser-local LLM instance/worker**, processing generation jobs sequentially (not ten simultaneous GPU models or remote API calls), with strict per-session budgets and graceful failure handling.
- The app remains static GitHub Pages hosting: IndexedDB and cached browser-local WebLLM, no backend, external AI API, ongoing paid service, real multi-user connectivity or historical user impersonation.

## Context

Current `main` (reinspect before implementation):
- `src/ai/personas.ts`: fixed `星守` (`hoshimori`), `草笛` (`kusabue`), `半田ごて` (`hankote`) and their stable `fictional-ai:<id>` member IDs. **Preserve their IDs and already-saved posts**; add seven new original residents.
- `src/ai/activity.ts`: global `maxPosts=0` default, `Math.floor(elapsed/HOUR)` cap and index-based rotation of the three personas/boards.
- `src/ai/activity-runner.ts`, `src/ai/controls.ts`: a single bounded reconnect batch and manual generation, stored batch/run statuses, cancellation, and retries. `src/main.ts` calls activity on startup/reconnect; a visible-minute timer currently only updates last activity time.
- `src/ai/generation.ts`: bounded same-forum recent-post context; validated JSON output. `src/storage/repository.ts` transactionally persists identities, posts, and run IDs. `src/storage/schema.ts` validates current version-1 backups and activity settings.
- Existing local SIGs and forums, historical navigation and `src/settings.ts` must continue working. AI must not write fake system messages or modify menus. Previous implementation docs: [local AI behavior](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/docs/local-ai.md).
- [Contribution and review guidance](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md): write new Issue/PR/docs text in English; user-visible product text stays Japanese.

### Resident behavior design

Define ten **original** period-style fictional residents in a small, data-driven profile format. Retain the existing three identities and introduce seven more; choose seven varied roles (e.g. office worker, shop clerk, student, caregiver/night-shift worker, teacher, software hobbyist, hobby photographer) with different hour/day availability, interests, tone, and reply likelihood. These are character fiction, **not** factual portrayals of actual historical PC-VAN users.

For each resident, maintain:

- Stable ID, handle, occupation, short biography, personality / writing style, topic interests, preferred SIGs/boards.
- A meaningful local daily routine (weekday/weekend, sleep/work/study or shift windows, and time zone or an explicit common local time zone), a baseline **participation propensity**, and separate probabilities/weights for reading, new threads, replies and intentional inactivity. **A work schedule affects activity, but does not rigidly forbid all exceptions.**
- A small optional relationship/affinity map and bounded memory of prior **local** discussion/replies, so AI participants may return to topics and address each other consistently.
- Individual editable controls (handle, job/routine, active hours, frequency/activity level, preferred boards, reply propensity, interests) and a separate overall activity level/pause switch. Store validated settings in IndexedDB and include them in backup/restore. Defaults should produce varied but not constant activity.

Scheduling should derive due opportunities **per resident** from these profiles plus discussion triggers. It must allow genuine zero-post intervals, people disappearing for a few days, varied times, occasional new topics, and replies to relevant human **or AI** posts. Use reproducible seeded random decisions with injected clock/seed for tests rather than every persona always posting in sequence; respect time zone and weekday/weekend boundaries. The LLM is used to **write** a selected action; deterministic scheduling controls who/when/where/reply-to within a bounded budget.

### Important defaults and network consent

- A **new** local world has resident auto-activity configured **ON** with conservative global per-session work limits; the user can turn it off entirely and adjust residents separately. The default must not be an apparently-active switch that never schedules anything.
- Browser-local WebLLM's initial download may be hundreds of MB to GB. **Do not automatically download heavy model files or start unexpected network inference on first visit.** Show a concise, explicit first-use model-download consent/setup step under Settings (optionally a small nonintrusive notice). Until the user authorizes it, the residents are scheduled/ready but no inference runs; accurately indicate “AI setup required” rather than pretending they posted. Once the user explicitly consents and a compatible model is available, auto activity works without further manual post-generation clicks, including subsequent visits. Allow pause/unload and preserve normal terminal use when unsupported.
- Automatically seed/create a **small set of writable local forums** corresponding to the existing documented SIG destinations when first needed, so an empty first-time user does **not** need to create a human member or manual post before AI can start. Do **not** insert fictional posts as historical records, overwrite imported worlds, or resurrect demo messages in an intentionally empty local board.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] New local worlds contain ten distinct seeded fictional resident profiles, all inspectable and individually editable with stable IDs. Keep original `hoshimori`, `kusabue`, `hankote` identities and previously saved AI/human posts intact; seven added residents have distinct realistic jobs, lifestyle schedules, voices, interests and connection habits. Edits persist across reload and versioned JSON backup/restore; invalid settings are rejected safely.
- [ ] New worlds default to **automatic resident activity ON**, subject to a clear **one-time explicit consent** before downloading heavyweight model data. After model setup, the user can just open the app, read/write posts and see residents participate without pressing “generate” or reconnecting. Global pause/disable and per-resident frequency/schedule customization work. Existing users' saved choices are preserved, including explicitly disabled auto activity.
- [ ] Provide usable, writable local board(s) for automatic residents even in an otherwise clean browser profile; preserve the historical SIG/menu fixtures and locally imported/customized forums. The user must not have to submit an initial human post just to enable AI.
- [ ] Replace global `one post per hour` / round-robin persona scheduling with **independent per-resident schedules** driven by routine, day/time, interests, activity propensity and current board context. Each resident may decide to stay silent. Realistic activity changes between daytime/nighttime and workdays/weekends; use bounded deterministic random sources for repeatable tests. No claim that simulated output follows a verified historical timeline.
- [ ] When the tab stays open, due residents can independently generate posts over time, including after a human post; **do not reply to every message immediately**. A scheduled response should reflect that person's own availability. No inference occurs while browser is closed; on re-open, catch up with a bounded subset of missed activities in chronological order, without requiring `RECONNECT`. Leave the terminal responsive throughout.
- [ ] AI residents can reply to **each other's** previously committed messages as well as local human messages and can start new topics. Replies retain valid same-forum `replyToPostId` relations. Bounded recent conversation/memory and individual interests/relationships influence the selected target and generated tone, rather than ten generic independent posts. The user can inspect the origin and persona profile on demand, not via intrusive historical-screen disclaimers.
- [ ] Use **one shared local model worker** with a sequential or otherwise safely serialized inference queue, bounded prompt lengths, per-visit attempts/post caps and a conservative default global generation budget. No multi-model GPU explosion, hidden network inference, infinite loops or uncontrolled catch-up after weeks of absence. Catch-up may be truncated with understandable status rather than fabricating every missed hour. Generation/cancellation/offline/WebGPU errors do not block menus, human posting, backups or navigation.
- [ ] Persist durable per-resident next-due/activity state and idempotent run identifiers so reloads, repeated visibility events, interrupted generation, two tabs and retries neither double-post nor generate an unbounded queue. Preserve actual commit time separately from fictional scheduled time. Changes to settings should safely recalculate future activity without rewriting past posts; logical event order should be maintained.
- [ ] Maintain backward compatibility with existing IndexedDB data, existing `ai-activity` settings and version-1 backup files. Implement an explicit, validated migration or additive schema design; do not discard pending work silently or reset users' previously saved opt-in/opt-out settings. Restore/import should remain atomic, and stable AI identity IDs must survive migration.
- [ ] Preserve useful manual AI preview/save functionality, optional WebLLM model selection, provenance fields and current local-only constraints. Do not generate historical menu text, import archives as AI memory, create real network participants or remove AI attribution from Settings/backup.
- [ ] Add automated tests with a fake clock, fixed PRNG seed and mocked LLM covering all ten personas, varying daily routines/timezones, quiet periods, an always-open tab, delayed response to user posts, AI-to-AI replies, first-use defaults/consent, no-initial-user-post bootstrapping, cross-tab/restart idempotency, catch-up caps, pause/resume, profile edit persistence, old-backup migration and GPU/model failures. No real GPU/model downloads are required.
- [ ] Update README, local-AI documentation and settings help with the new resident model, real-time-vs-catch-up distinction, model download requirements, settings controls, limitations and tested commands. Run `npm test`/build and applicable validation; report failures/skips honestly in the PR.

## Optional validation

On a supported local WebGPU desktop, manually observe the ten-person community over several real open/close/reopen cycles, including gradual AI-to-AI conversation and character consistency. This subjective/hardware-dependent validation is useful but **not a mandatory pre-merge gate**.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. All acceptance criteria can be tested against the built browser app locally with deterministic clocks, repository fixtures and mocked models. GitHub Pages publication may be monitored separately under the existing deployment workflow but is not a pre-merge completion gate.
